criteria.rationale: Examined the memo key and Git invocation. Verified: replace refs and grafts disabled for every governance Git call (git_snapshot_integrity.go:579), linked worktrees/submodules skipped (.git must be a directory), shallow and repo config stamps in the key, hits admitted against the operation budget, hosted checks resolve root from the Git toplevel and take no caller-relative paths. Unresolved: user/global Git config not in the key (recorded low follow-up). Accepted: env digest is an allow-list; the speed-up is measured by hand.

Memo mutations under a mutex; one hosted command at a time via a semaphore with the deadline covering the queue wait; a command past its deadline counted by Busy in idle, drain and status; covered under -race.
Request exported within an internal package; new Reply fields omitempty so slice-1 replies are unchanged; pose.runtime.run/1 is new and documented; the slice-1 runtime contract evidence still passes.
The memo hook in capture is inert unless enabled; read-view and pure-read audit integration still pass.
Refusals, deadlines and unknown outcomes carry bounded typed reasons; the envelope reports via, fallback_reason, outcome, epoch and per-command memo_hits.

Examined runtime_cmd.go, runtime.go and cli.go help: without run and with the memo off by default nothing changes; status, stop and attach keep error matching because OutcomeUnknownError unwraps; help and manuals add run. Concluded compatible.

Read the handler, client and memo; the round-1/2/4 fixes are present (partial reply unknown, 2 MiB output bound, Busy count, per-command hits, config stamp, runtime-side refusal, queued command withdrawn).

D1 (basis R5, R7, R10): measurement put the remaining cost in Git (about 14 s of 242 log -1 calls); reads pure in a commit or object id need no freshness proof because the commit is the key, and hosting gives the process lifetime the memo needs. The structure matches: memo in internal/pose, protocol in worktreeruntime, handler in cli.

Examined runtimeRunUnknown and the refusal reasons: a command that never started falls back with a stated reason, and a command that may have run exits 1 telling the operator to check its effects before rerunning. Concluded actionable.
Each of R5, R7 and R10 is traced to tests included in this check's -run pattern.
Compared the diff with the spec artifact list and non-goals: only the five checks are hosted, run is explicit, and there is no admission/QoS. Concluded in scope.

Examined the endpoint and handler: 0600 socket with the peer uid checked before reading; unhosted commands and a different environment digest are refused before start; same user and worktree as standalone, so no authority gain; bounded request and reply sizes.

The smallest alternative (hosting without a memo) gives no gain per the measurement; the memo is 115 lines limited to the already-classified pure reads, with no speculative extension points; D1 names the falsifier. The memory accounting gap is F3 (low).

findings.action: Replace the literal \n\n with a real blank line in the four manuals and keep the parity test green.
findings.rationale: The hosted-checks paragraph ends with a literal \n\n and absorbs the 'Review rounds' paragraph; same defect in locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:944 and both scaffold dist copies (shipped to installed projects).

findings.action: Treat a reply with Error and empty Outcome as a refusal (fallback standalone) and add a test with an oversized request.
findings.rationale: A runtime reply carrying only Error and no outcome (e.g. a request over 64 KiB rejected as invalid JSON at runtime.go:410) certainly did not start the command, yet the default branch reports it unknown and exits 1 instead of falling back standalone as the spec constraint requires.

findings.action: Add a fixed per-entry overhead to the accounted size or restate the bound in D1 and the manual.
findings.rationale: The memo byte budget counts only key+stdout, not per-entry list/map/struct overhead, so the 256 MiB stated in D1 understates resident memory when entries are small (the common 41-byte log -1 output).

findings.action: Document the 10-minute cap in the four manuals or refuse a larger --timeout with a usage error.
findings.rationale: A --timeout above MaxHostedDuration (10 min) is silently cut to 10 min on both ends; the manuals do not state the cap, so a caller can get an unknown outcome earlier than the timeout it asked for.
